text:
Sophie: FYI — shifting the planned EU-west1 maintenance window by ~45m. Need a quick review + customer copy. New window: 2026-03-16 09:45–10:15 UTC (was 09:00–09:30). Reason: upstream firmware validation delayed the node drains until the warm-migration finishes. Expected impact: rolling serving-node drains in eu-west1; short elevated tail latencies (~5–12s) for embeddings and chat, and brief reduced throughput for a subset of requests. No data loss expected. Oncall: @Gabe to lead. If we get a +1 here, we'll publish to status page and CS at 09:15 UTC. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/node-drain-euw1 Please ACK.

Ops-Bot: automation note — maintenance schedule change recorded. Will keep pager schedule unchanged. Will post statuspage draft to #statuspage-drafts in 10m and queue the customer email for review.

Gabe: ACK and taking point. I'll be on the bridge. Devon — can you validate fallback routing to the smaller instance pool and confirm KV cache warmup expectations? I'll prepare a 10% canary and a fallback rollout policy (automatic rollback if error rate >2% for 2m).

Devon: Confirmed — canary route exists. KV cache warmup looks ok but expect a short period of cache miss amplification during drains. Recommend disabling continuous batching for the canary to avoid request batching timeouts. Also suggest adding a 2 minute grace window to the rollout to avoid noisy signals from autoscaler bursts.

Maria (CS): Customer-facing draft below. Plain language, short. Please edit/approve.

```
Subject: Short planned maintenance in EU-west1 — 16 Mar 2026

Hi there,

We're doing a brief planned maintenance in our EU-west1 region on 16 Mar 2026 starting at 09:45 UTC. During the 30-minute window you may see briefly elevated response times for some requests and transient reduced throughput. There is no expected data loss and no action needed from you.

We'll post live updates on our status page: https://status.redwood.ai and follow up with a summary after completion.

Thanks,
Redwood Inference Operations
```

OpsComm: Small wording suggestions — soften "transient reduced throughput" to "briefly reduced throughput for some requests" (Maria's draft already does this). Add a link to support@redwood.ai and a note "If you have a dedicated SLA contact, we'll reach out directly if we expect any customer-specific impact." Also: include an estimated time for the follow-up summary (within 1 hour post-maint).

Sophie: Updated status page draft — please :thumbsup: if good. Posting schedule: draft->09:15 UTC customer email, 09:20 UTC status page publish, 09:35 bridge up, 09:45 start drains, 10:05 expected completion, final statuspage at ~10:15. Statuspage snippet below.

```
Scheduled Maintenance — EU-west1
Start: 2026-03-16 09:45 UTC
Expected duration: 30 minutes
Impact: During this maintenance window, users in EU-west1 may experience briefly elevated latencies and reduced throughput for some requests. No data loss is expected. We will provide updates here and a post-maint summary.
Updated: Sophie (Operations)
```

Oncall-Bot: PagerSimulation scheduled 2026-03-16 09:40 UTC to validate oncall bridge readiness. This is informational and will not send pages outside the oncall rotation.

Gabe: Final plan: I'll post the customer email at 09:15 UTC. OpsComm, please stand by to post the status page at 09:20 UTC. Devon and I will be on the bridge at 09:35. Handoff: Gabe -> Devon for active mitigation. If we hit severity S1 (service-wide failures) escalate to EngSRE and page the CTL channel. I'll be monitoring metrics and will call rollback if error spikes exceed our threshold.

Sophie: Post-maint update (10:05 UTC): maintenance completed early. All serving nodes returned, KV caches warmed, tail latencies back to baseline. No customer-facing incidents detected in the monitoring windows. Posting final statuspage update and sending the follow-up email to customers now. Huge thanks to the oncall + ops folks for the quick coordination. :party_parrot:

(Opinionated notes/replay for the archive)
- Keep explicit line in customer copy: "No data loss expected" — customers care more about that than jargon.
- Ops: consider adding short KB item on the status page describing what "cache warmup" looks like for embedding workloads.

(reacts: :thumbsup: x4 from Gabe, Devon, OpsComm, Maria)
